dispositionDefinitions.implemented_pending_integrated_verificat: The scoped implementation and focused evidence exist in the working tree, but the final integrated gate is not recorded.
dispositionDefinitions.partial_pending_integrated_verification: A bounded, truthfully labeled implementation exists, but part of the intended product capability or its required environment proof is still missing.
dispositionDefinitions.verified_local_worktree: The remediation passed focused, integrated and applicable browser or contract verification in the current uncommitted working tree.
dispositionDefinitions.verified_local_pending_external_gate: The repository remediation passed local verification, while a live provider, crawler, proxy, database, container or assistive-technology gate remains external to this checkout.
dispositionDefinitions.open: No complete remediation is present in the current working tree.
dispositionDefinitions.external_configuration_blocker: The remediation is outside this repository and requires a live external configuration change plus re-verification.

localCandidate.qualityGate: a fresh complete isolated run passed after the bounded Cloudflare provider and edge-header changes
localCandidate.coverage: 412 tests passed with 92.72% statements, 84.54% branches, 93.54% functions, and 93.73% lines across the configured critical-file denominator; thresholds remain 92%, 84%, 93%, and 93%
localCandidate.performanceTests: 2 passed; 250 representative simulations and five bounded solves remained within separate two-second measured budgets
localCandidate.build: passed; 4,886 web modules transformed and 25 offline assets prepared
localCandidate.browserEvidence: Edge 151 passed 17 desktop, mobile, completed and warmed-offline route audits at 1440x900 and 390x844; authoring, privacy, run controls, intervention, fork, completion, trace playback, candidate-safe Run library persistence and portable replay passed with zero unexpected console/network errors, acceptance defects or document overflow
localCandidate.hardeningEvidence: All four targeted mutants were killed; serial and parallel fixed-seed 52-file, 412-test stability passes completed without retry
localCandidate.dependencyAudit: pnpm production audit reported no known vulnerabilities
localCandidate.independentAcceptance: no surviving source-confirmed or browser-confirmed P0-P2 finding

hostedProduction.evidence: The live hostname serves an older engine 0.3.0 build with stale routing, SPA HTML at crawl and asset-manifest URLs, a stale web manifest with the wrong MIME type, service-worker v3 and the old blueprint PNG; a Cloudflare challenge-platform loader conflicts with the strict application CSP.
requiredBeforeGo: commit and run protected CI and immutable-image gates for the exact reviewed revision
obtain explicit owner authorization before deployment
disable or nonce-integrate Cloudflare script injection without weakening CSP
deploy the exact tested revision and purge affected special URL caches
publish revision evidence and repeat the live route, header, mobile, offline and canonical-run audit

currentMitigations: Shared-scenario creation defaults to 10 per IP per day, new records expire after 30 days, and expired rows are removed before capacity accounting.
Canonical polling is revision-bound and cannot attach an old run status or digest after scenario or architecture edits.
Replay hashes are described as internal consistency checks and not author authentication.
Known and unknown routes, shared-link noindex, crawl assets, manifest MIME, service-worker API bypass, and immutable 404 cache behavior have repository contracts.
The local UI covers every main route and has evidence-linked sampled-trace path playback tied to real modeled spans.

The optional AI provider boundary is disabled by default; the production profile pins Cloudflare Workers AI gpt-oss-20b behind 10 daily reservations, a 400-cent application ceiling and a required 450-cent Gateway spend limit, but no real provider transaction or retention configuration was exercised.
HTML responses emit Cache-Control no-transform so Cloudflare cannot inject scripts into the strict self-only CSP document; the live hostname still requires verification after promotion.
knownLocalLimitations: The manifest has no safe-zone-tested maskable application icon.
The Edge offline gate used a warmed service worker; a first-install cold PWA and every lazy worker on a physical device were not exercised.
No target-device Core Web Vitals profile or complete screen-reader certification was run.
Docker-backed Compose, Caddy-container, PostgreSQL, image-scan and full integration gates await protected CI because the local Docker daemon was unavailable.
The optional AI boundary was tested with fake providers only and no real provider retention or billing path was exercised.

historicalFindings.title: Topology wiring did not materially execute request paths
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Every architecture run, comparison, request-class route, cache path, and asynchronous dependency lane
evidence: The gap audit produced byte-identical output after materially redirecting asynchronous traffic and swapping cache/database order.
The current worktree adds directed demand propagation and route validation in packages/sim-core/src/simulate.ts.
Focused regressions are defined in packages/sim-core/tests/topology-execution.test.ts and packages/sim-core/tests/request-class-execution.test.ts.
historicalFindings.rootCause: The previous engine allocated demand mainly by component kind and used edges as coarse reachability metadata instead of an executable source-to-target graph.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Execute workload demand through directed edges with deterministic traffic shares, explicit request-class routes, synchronous and asynchronous boundaries, cache effects, retries, transport loss, latency, and route validation.
requiredTests: redirecting an asynchronous source changes downstream demand
cache-before-database differs from database-before-cache
serial and parallel paths differ
disconnected components receive no executed demand
traffic shares change downstream demand
invalid request-class routes fail closed
retry work remains on the failed dependency path

measurements.before: Materially different graphs produced byte-identical SimulationResult output.
measurements.after: Engine 0.7.0 executes directed, class-aware topology demand and passed the adversarial topology matrix plus the integrated 398-test gate.

independentReview.summary: Independent engine review reran the adversarial route, fan-out, cache, regional, failure and durability cases; the focused and integrated gates passed.

historicalFindings.title: Obsolete local workers could publish stale telemetry
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Users who edit, reset, switch scenarios, or start another run while local simulation is active
evidence: The previous local worker returned one unversioned terminal result that the store accepted unconditionally.
apps/web/src/lib/localSimulation.ts and apps/web/src/workers/simulation.worker.ts now attach run, scenario revision, architecture revision, and input IDs to every command and response.
apps/web/tests/local-simulation.test.ts and apps/web/tests/local-run-store.test.ts cover cancellation, supersession, stale response rejection, streaming equivalence, and reveal isolation.
historicalFindings.rootCause: The worker protocol had no run identity, revision guard, cancellation lifecycle, or identified streaming batches.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Use revision-bound run identities on every message; terminate or ignore superseded runs; stream deterministic frame/event batches; and reveal interview criteria only for the still-current completed server run.
requiredTests: stale result and batch rejection
explicit cancellation terminates the worker
a new run supersedes the old run
architecture and scenario edits invalidate an active run
streamed batches equal the final simulation result
interview reveal cannot follow an obsolete run

measurements.before: No local run identity or revision guard existed and no frames were delivered before completion.
measurements.after: The protocol exposes identified batches and session states with store-side current-run guards; stale, cancel, fork and replay paths passed the integrated gate and browser workflow.

independentReview.summary: Identity, cancellation, stale-result and replay lifecycle paths passed focused, integrated and browser verification.

historicalFindings.title: Pre-run and absent evidence states were presented as healthy measurements
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: All users before their first run, after an edit, or when a result omits optional evidence
evidence: Nodes without metrics previously defaulted to healthy, zero latency/RPS, and 100 percent availability.
apps/web/src/components/ComponentNode.tsx, InspectorPanel.tsx, TelemetryPanel.tsx, and apps/web/src/pages/LabPage.tsx now render explicit not-run, pending, unavailable, and empty states.
apps/web/tests/inspector.test.tsx and apps/web/tests/telemetry.test.tsx distinguish not-run, streaming, omitted traces, explicit empty traces, and zero-span samples.
historicalFindings.rootCause: Missing results and optional evidence were collapsed into numeric and health defaults.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Represent not-run, loading, unsupported evidence, confirmed empty evidence, and completed results as distinct states; use em dashes instead of invented metrics.
requiredTests: component and inspector not-run rendering
no pre-run health score or availability
streaming state does not imply final scoring
optional evidence omitted differs from an explicit empty collection

measurements.before: Healthy, 100 percent, and zero-value outputs appeared without a run.
measurements.after: The worktree uses not-run labels and em dashes, preserves omitted-versus-empty trace evidence, and passed route, component, Inspector and Telemetry acceptance.

independentReview.summary: A trace-specific review corrected the omitted-versus-empty ambiguity; focused, integrated and real-browser evidence states passed.

historicalFindings.title: Operational evidence and controls were not reliably usable at supported viewports or by keyboard
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Laptop, mobile, keyboard-only, reduced-motion, and screen-reader Lab users
evidence: The audit found hidden clock, seed, run state, global health, and linked-event evidence at desktop breakpoints, plus unreadably shrunken mobile topology text.

The worktree adds a persistent mobile state strip, compact topology viewport behavior, non-inert graph-lint rows, controlled multi-selection, command-palette keyboard behavior, trace roving selection, focus treatment, and reduced-motion rules.
Focused behavior tests exist in apps/web/tests/command-palette.test.tsx, lab-selection.test.ts, telemetry.test.tsx, and architecture-lint.test.ts.
historicalFindings.rootCause: Responsive rules removed essential state and scaled the desktop graph down; several custom controls lacked complete keyboard and semantic behavior.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Keep critical state visible, use a readable typography floor and focused mobile viewport, preserve linked evidence, and provide complete keyboard, focus, live-region, and reduced-motion behavior.
requiredTests: 1440 by 900 operational-state and linked-event browser capture
390 by 844 readable topology and no document overflow
keyboard-only build, run, trace, lint, and palette workflows
screen-reader semantics and reduced-motion behavior

measurements.before: Essential state was hidden at two desktop breakpoints and mobile fit reduced node text to only a few rendered pixels.
measurements.after: Edge passed desktop and 390x844 layout, 12 px operational text, 40 px primary touch targets, keyboard, focus and reduced-motion checks; screen-reader certification remains unexecuted.

independentReview.summary: Focused accessibility regressions and the tracked Edge desktop/mobile gate passed; a complete screen-reader or physical-device certification is not claimed.

historicalFindings.title: User-facing copy overstated live, measured, verified, trace, and causal evidence
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Visitors, candidates, interviewers, and anyone interpreting a local or server result
evidence: The copy audit found live language for deterministic playback, verified language for server recomputation, trace language for aggregate histories, and causal language stronger than the event evidence.
Primary routes and workbench surfaces now use modeled run, sampled request trace, linked event, server run, server-backed session, and scheduled incident terminology.
apps/web/src/lib/evidenceReport.ts now marks unmet pre-run objectives as NOT RUN rather than failed evidence.
historicalFindings.rootCause: Mission-control wording drifted beyond the simulator's actual evidence and trust boundaries.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Keep modeled versus observed, local versus server-backed, aggregate versus sampled, and linked versus proven-causal terminology consistent across routes, reports, loading, error, and offline states.
requiredTests: route and overlay copy smoke
local versus server-backed terminology review
generated report wording review
loading, error, empty, offline, and replay-boundary copy review

measurements.before: Overstated terms appeared across home, Lab, studios, overlays, reports, and offline states.
measurements.after: Primary and generated copy uses explicit local, server-backed, sampled, modeled and internal-consistency boundaries; route and browser review passed.

independentReview.summary: The route/copy matrix, trace truthfulness review, replay authenticity wording and final browser route audit passed.

historicalFindings.title: Search metadata, crawl surfaces, route status, and static delivery were incomplete
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Search crawlers, shared-link recipients, installable-app users, and first-load visitors
evidence: The baseline lacked robots.txt and sitemap.xml, used static page metadata, treated unknown Sites paths as successful app-shell responses, and shipped a 1.21 MB blueprint PNG.

The worktree adds apps/web/src/components/RouteMetadata.tsx, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, known-route versus real-404 handling in the Sites worker and nginx, explicit manifest and JSON MIME rules, and a 14,640-byte WebP blueprint.
Sites returns the branded application shell with HTTP 404 for unknown HTML routes; nginx returns a genuine generic 404 for unknown paths rather than a soft 404.
Focused coverage is defined in apps/web/tests/route-metadata.test.tsx and apps/web/tests/sites-worker.test.mjs.
historicalFindings.rootCause: The SPA shell had no route-aware metadata or crawl assets and its fallback rules did not distinguish real client routes from unknown paths.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Publish crawl files, set route-aware metadata and noindex rules, return a real 404 for unknown paths, preserve 200 app-shell fallback only for known routes, and optimize large static assets.
requiredTests: known route returns the app shell with status 200
unknown Sites route returns the branded shell with status 404 and unknown nginx route returns a genuine 404
shared routes are noindex
robots, sitemap, manifest, and optimized background fetch with correct MIME types
production crawler check with and without JavaScript

measurements.before: Blueprint PNG was 1.21 MB; crawl files were absent; unknown Sites routes became soft 404s.
measurements.after: Blueprint WebP is 14,640 bytes; repository route, crawl, MIME, noindex and Sites tests passed; deployed crawler and proxy responses remain a production gate.

independentReview.summary: Route metadata, seven Sites delivery tests and generated offline assets passed; deployed response and crawler behavior are not recorded for this working tree.

historicalFindings.title: Cloudflare-injected analytics conflicts with the production CSP
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Public visitors and operators relying on a clean production security console
evidence: The live audit reproduced CSP errors for a Cloudflare-injected script that is not present in this repository.
The repository CSP intentionally keeps script-src restricted to self and does not add unsafe-inline.
historicalFindings.rootCause: An external Cloudflare feature injects a script that is not authorized by the origin's strict CSP.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Disable the Cloudflare injection or authorize only the exact script through a supported nonce or hash without weakening the general script policy.
requiredTests: production browser console has no CSP violations
script-src remains free of unsafe-inline and broad third-party origins

measurements.before: CSP violations were reproduced on the live deployment.
measurements.after: No repository change can resolve the injected script; a Cloudflare change and live retest remain required.

independentReview.summary: The failure was observed live and traced outside the repository.

historicalFindings.title: Live interventions, replay, snapshot, and fork semantics needed an honest execution boundary
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Users pausing a local run, scheduling an outage or policy change, replaying evidence, or branching a completed run
evidence: The previous worker exposed only a final immutable result and could not accept run controls or intervention commands.

The current protocol supports pause, resume, step, speed, finish, bounded future interventions, deterministic snapshots, replay, and fork fingerprints in apps/web/src/workers/simulation.worker.ts and apps/web/src/lib/completedRun.ts.

The manifest records engine/input identity, revisions, seed, digest, action schedule, selected delivered frame, and the explicit no-opaque-state boundary; focused tests are in local-simulation.test.ts, completed-run.test.ts, local-run-store.test.ts, and packages/sim-core/tests/interventions.test.ts.
historicalFindings.rootCause: The simulator computed a whole result and had no session protocol, action schedule, resumable evidence artifact, or vocabulary separating replay from serialized runtime state.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Allow only future actions while paused; recompute deterministically from second zero; reject any changed delivered prefix; bind replays to identical inputs, actions, and result digest; and label snapshots/forks as replay provenance rather than restored in-flight physics.
requiredTests: future action preserves every delivered frame and event
past, invalid, stale, and over-capacity actions fail closed
pause, resume, step, speed, finish, and cancel preserve run identity
snapshot restoration replays from zero and matches fingerprints
completed replay verifies identical inputs, action schedule, and result digest
manifest export excludes private interview content

measurements.before: No run controls, action schedule, manifest, replay proof, snapshot, or fork foundation existed.
measurements.after: Bounded paused-run recomputation and deterministic replay/fork evidence are present; true serialized mid-run engine state and arbitrary live topology mutation remain absent.

independentReview.summary: Prefix preservation, action scheduling, snapshot/fork, portable replay, digest comparison and the no-opaque-state boundary passed focused, integrated and browser verification.

historicalFindings.title: Architecture editing lacked safe bulk operations, coherent history, and configuration preservation
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Users connecting, selecting, moving, duplicating, deleting, clearing, laying out, undoing, or restoring architectures
evidence: The audit found destructive whole-edge rewrites, incomplete multi-selection behavior, no coherent undo/redo flow, and no recoverable blank draft.

apps/web/src/lib/architectureEditing.ts and useLabStore.ts now provide additive connection, mixed node/edge deletion, internal-link duplication, deterministic layout, blank drafts, bounded undo/redo, named snapshots, and coalesced transient drag commits.
Focused regressions exist in architecture-editing.test.ts, architecture-history.test.ts, lab-selection.test.ts, share.test.ts, inspector.test.tsx, and architecture-lint.test.ts.
historicalFindings.rootCause: Editor actions were implemented as unrelated component callbacks without shared immutable operations, controlled selection state, or a bounded history contract.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Centralize immutable editing operations, preserve untouched edge/node configuration, track controlled node and edge selection, coalesce drag history, permit an empty persisted editor draft, and block runs with actionable graph lint.
requiredTests: new links do not strip existing transport configuration
mixed selection deletion removes connected links exactly once
duplicate copies only internal links and all nested configuration
undo and redo round-trip one logical drag as one step
blank drafts hydrate and share without becoming runnable submissions
node, edge, and non-actionable lint items route correctly

measurements.before: Editing could lose link configuration and offered no coherent multi-selection, history, or recoverable blank state.
measurements.after: Editor operations, persistence, history, selection, lint routing and the browser authoring/share workflow passed.

independentReview.summary: Editor, history, selection, Inspector and graph-lint tests passed, and Edge completed local authoring, sharing and Lab interaction.

historicalFindings.title: Aggregate charts did not expose bounded request-path observability
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Users investigating routing, retries, cache decisions, queue lineage, database waits, and modeled failures
evidence: The product previously exposed aggregate frame histories but called some of that evidence traces.
Engine 0.7.0 emits optional deterministic SampledTrace and SampledSpan records capped at 16 traces and 64 spans per trace.

apps/web/src/components/TelemetryPanel.tsx exposes executed node/edge order, parent lineage, retry attempts, cache decisions, asynchronous message lineage, query class, inferred connection-pool wait, failure cause, and explicit sampled-not-exhaustive boundaries; telemetry.test.tsx covers selection and empty states.
historicalFindings.rootCause: The result contract had aggregate node/edge metrics only and the UI lacked a bounded request-class explanation surface.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Emit deterministic representative request-class spans from executed paths and render an accessible selector and modeled span sequence without claiming captured production traces or chronology unsupported by timestamps.
requiredTests: a real simulated request class yields spans from its executed edge order
retry, cache, async message, query, pool-wait, and failure fields render
trace and span caps are enforced deterministically
undefined traces differ from an explicit empty array
keyboard selection exposes visible inline detail
sampled and inferred limitations remain adjacent to the evidence

measurements.before: Only aggregate histories were available and trace wording overstated their granularity.
measurements.after: Bounded request samples, trace exploration and graph-linked discrete playback are present and passed the real-simulation browser workflow.

independentReview.summary: Independent review corrected evidence states and wording; telemetry regressions plus keyboard, reduced-motion and Edge path playback passed.

historicalFindings.title: Robustness analysis blocked the UI and lacked bounded cancellation and stale-result handling
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Users running multi-seed robustness comparisons from the Decision Workbench
evidence: The previous Decision Workbench evaluated robustness synchronously on the UI thread.

apps/web/src/lib/robustnessAnalysis.ts and apps/web/src/workers/robustness.worker.ts add a dedicated worker, deterministic between-seed progress, request/input identity, cancellation, work-unit admission, and wall-clock limits.

apps/web/tests/robustness-analysis.test.ts and decision-workbench-robustness.test.tsx cover equivalent completion, cancellation, stale completion, timeout, over-budget, worker error, and no-result UI.
historicalFindings.rootCause: Multi-seed simulation was called directly from React without a worker lifecycle or bounded admission protocol.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Run robustness work in a dedicated worker with revision-bound identity, deterministic progress, immediate session cancellation, and explicit no-result/error states under wall-clock or work-unit limits.
requiredTests: worker output equals the established robustness calculation
progress is deterministic between seeds
cancel terminates the session without publishing a result
stale revision response is ignored
wall-clock and work-unit limits produce no result
UI error and retry states remain accessible

measurements.before: Nine seeded simulations could occupy the browser UI thread with no cancellation or progress boundary.
measurements.after: The work runs off-thread with progress between seeds; one synchronous seed is interruptible only by terminating the Worker, not cooperatively inside simulate().

independentReview.summary: Completion, progress, cancellation, timeout, budget, stale response and no-result semantics passed focused and integrated build verification.

historicalFindings.title: Cold offline use and origin failure fallback did not include the complete Lab runtime
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Returning users during network or origin failure, cold PWA installs, and operators testing degraded delivery
evidence: The previous service worker cached only a small shell list and did not guarantee lazy route or worker bundles were available offline.

apps/web/public/sw.js and prepare-sites-build.mjs now generate and install an asset precache containing built JavaScript, CSS, WebP, selected fonts, and worker chunks, while preserving real client errors.

deploy/nginx.conf adds explicit offline handling and deploy/Caddyfile.systemforge.open adds a no-store branded 503 fallback; service_worker_contract.test.mjs, sites-worker.test.mjs, and edge_contract.test.sh define focused checks.
The final build prepared 25 offline assets; service-worker, edge and all seven Sites behavior tests passed, and Edge loaded Lab, Scenario, Interview and Replay from a warmed offline cache.
historicalFindings.rootCause: The offline cache was a handwritten shell list and neither proxy layer had a fully tested, truthfully worded application fallback contract.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Generate the offline asset list from the build, bind cache writes to service-worker event lifetime, bypass API requests, fall back only for network and 5xx failures, and return branded no-store 503 content from Caddy/nginx.
requiredTests: warmed offline Lab, Scenario, Interview and Replay routes load from the generated precache
API requests never fall back to cached HTML
4xx responses remain visible rather than becoming offline content
5xx navigation uses cached Lab when available
Caddy and nginx return no-store branded 503 content
installed service worker upgrades without a mixed-version cache

measurements.before: The cache did not guarantee the lazy Lab and worker runtime for a cold offline session.
measurements.after: Generated precache, API bypass, lazy route/worker packaging and warmed real-browser offline routes passed; deployed Caddy/nginx failover remains a production-host gate.

independentReview.summary: Service-worker, edge, Sites packaging and warmed Edge offline navigation passed; deployed proxy failover, mixed-version upgrade and a physical first-install PWA cold-start remain unexecuted.

historicalFindings.title: Interviewer credentials and Sites HTML responses needed standard authorization and security-header handling
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Interviewer share links, controlled reveal and collaboration requests, and all HTML served through the Sites adapter
evidence: The browser and API previously used a custom x-systemforge-host-token header and existing Sites HTML responses did not receive the production security-header set.
apps/web/src/lib/api.ts and apps/api/src/app.ts now use a UUID Bearer credential and reject malformed or legacy credential headers.

apps/web/worker/index.js adds CSP, HSTS, COOP, permissions, referrer, nosniff, frame-denial, and Server-header removal to HTML responses; apps/api/tests/app.test.ts, apps/web/tests/share.test.ts, and sites-worker.test.mjs define focused coverage.
historicalFindings.rootCause: A bespoke credential header bypassed standard authorization handling and the Sites fallback adapter returned HTML without the origin security policy.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Keep the high-entropy token in the URL fragment, send it only as Authorization: Bearer, parse it strictly, fail closed without disclosing scenario existence, and apply the same HTML security policy on every Sites shell and fallback response.
requiredTests: valid Bearer credential restores interviewer role
missing, malformed, wrong, and legacy headers fail closed
participant requests never receive interviewer-only fields
all existing and fallback HTML responses receive security headers
static non-HTML assets do not receive an HTML CSP
proxy logs redact Authorization in the deployment environment

measurements.before: A custom host-token header was accepted and Sites HTML policy depended on the upstream asset response.
measurements.after: Strict Bearer parsing, role restoration, candidate projection, Sites HTML headers and noindex behavior passed; deployed proxy log-redaction remains a production gate.

independentReview.summary: API, browser privacy, Sites delivery and final Edge interviewer/candidate flows passed; live proxy logging is not verified for this checkout.

historicalFindings.title: Interview reveal was not bound to a completed server run for the exact shared session
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Candidates and interviewers using after-run reveal policies or candidate-derived requirements
evidence: The previous milestone accepted an empty client declaration and local completion could attempt to advance reveal state.

Run submissions now persist sharedScenarioId and submitted inputs; /api/scenarios/:id/runs requires a UUID run, completed status, retained submission, exact share binding, matching public scenario, and the shared allowCandidateRequirements policy.

The browser records only a completed, still-current canonical run and preserves candidate-derived requirements without exposing hidden requirements or interviewer notes; focused API/store cases are in apps/api/tests/app.test.ts and apps/web/tests/local-run-store.test.ts.
historicalFindings.rootCause: The reveal milestone trusted a client-declared run event and retained no server-side submission binding to the specific shared interview.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Persist each run submission, bind it to the exact shared scenario, require retained completed server evidence, compare only public scenario data while enforcing candidate-authoring policy, and reject stale browser/session responses before reveal is applied.
requiredTests: local or client-declared completion cannot reveal
queued, failed, missing, expired, unrelated, and cross-share runs cannot reveal
identical public scenarios in different shares cannot reuse a run
candidate-derived requirements are accepted only when the shared policy permits them
hidden requirements, interviewer brief, and interviewer notes never enter candidate responses
session or scenario revision change rejects a late reveal response
real PostgreSQL JSONB submission round-trip and terminal-run eviction race fail closed

measurements.before: The milestone body carried no server run identity and was not tied to retained canonical input evidence.
measurements.after: Per-share completed-run binding, candidate policy and stale-browser race protection passed; a current real-PostgreSQL integration run remains blocked on Docker availability.

independentReview.summary: Adversarial API, memory-store, web race and browser privacy review found no surviving reveal bypass; exact-sha PostgreSQL integration remains a protected-CI gate.

historicalFindings.title: Private interview material was persisted in durable browser storage
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Interviewers opening private rubrics or collaboration sessions on shared or untrusted devices
evidence: apps/web/src/store/useLabStore.ts now writes only candidateScenario(...) to the persistent draft; hidden requirements and interviewerBrief cannot enter localStorage.
The full interviewer draft is retained only in tab-scoped sessionStorage, while a host token is accepted for refresh only after the server confirms interviewer role.

apps/web/tests/local-share-hydration.test.ts and apps/web/tests/share.test.ts cover participant transitions, invalid shares, role changes, candidate projections, and private-sentinel absence from durable storage.
historicalFindings.rootCause: Draft persistence treats public and interviewer-private scenario fields as one undifferentiated browser document.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Split public draft persistence from ephemeral interviewer-private state, avoid durable storage of hidden rubric content and bearer credentials where possible, clear private state on role/session changes, and document the remaining same-origin trust boundary.
requiredTests: participant and interviewer reloads preserve only the intended fields
hidden requirements and interviewer brief never enter durable localStorage
session switch and sign-out clear private artifacts and credentials
malformed persisted data fails closed without restoring private state

measurements.before: Full interviewer scenarios can be serialized under systemforge:draft and the host credential under systemforge:session.
measurements.after: Persistent drafts are candidate-safe; the necessary interviewer draft and confirmed host credential are tab-scoped and cleared on role/session invalidation.

independentReview.summary: The role-aware persistence split and fail-closed hydration paths passed focused privacy review and regression coverage.

historicalFindings.title: Local share decoding allowed unbounded decompression before rejection
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Anyone opening an untrusted local #share link
evidence: apps/web/src/lib/boundedLzString.ts enforces the decompressed-output limit while decoding instead of allocating an attacker-selected expanded string first.
Sensitive hash parameters are captured and scrubbed before React mounts; local payload decoding, JSON parsing, and Zod validation run in a disposable worker with a timeout.

apps/web/tests/bounded-lz-string.test.ts plus local-share hydration/share tests cover compressed bombs, malformed/truncated data, empty values, schema rejection, timeout, role transitions, and valid round trips.
historicalFindings.rootCause: Compressed local shares are decoded synchronously and the decisive expansion limit is enforced only after a complete decompressed string exists.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Move untrusted share decoding to a bounded disposable worker or adopt a format with enforceable streaming output limits; reduce input budgets and keep checksum and schema validation before hydration.
requiredTests: high-compression-ratio payload is rejected within memory and wall-clock budgets
oversized, corrupted, legacy, and unsupported-version links fail without changing the draft
valid versioned and blank-architecture shares still round-trip
decode cancellation prevents late hydration after route change

measurements.before: A 50,000-character compressed fragment can expand fully on the main thread before the decoded size is rejected.
measurements.after: Encoded and decompressed sizes are bounded before hydration, decoding is off the UI thread and timeout-bound, and late or invalid results fail closed.

independentReview.summary: The bounded decoder and worker hydration paths passed crafted high-compression and privacy regressions.

historicalFindings.title: Shared-session polling and mutations could apply responses out of order
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Candidates and interviewers using synchronized reveal, journal, cursor, and clock state
evidence: apps/web/src/store/useLabStore.ts now coalesces/aborts shared refreshes and serializes reveal/collaboration mutation admission.
Every response is guarded by the active share, confirmed role/credential, request identity, and mutation epoch before store publication.
apps/web/tests/local-run-store.test.ts and share tests cover late refresh/reveal/collaboration responses, same-session races, session replacement, and credential invalidation.
historicalFindings.rootCause: Shared-session reads and writes have no monotonic request identity, response version, abort lifecycle, or server revision token.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Use one abortable/coalesced poll per session, bind every mutation response to the current share, role, credential, and session revision, and add a server version or updatedAt compare-and-set contract for ordered collaboration updates.
requiredTests: older poll response cannot overwrite a newer response for the same share
session and role switch abort every old read and mutation
late reveal response cannot change a new session
concurrent collaboration edits have an explicit conflict policy
same-template session-switch race preserves privacy and local work

measurements.before: Overlapping polls and mutation responses have no ordering beyond a share-ID check on refresh.
measurements.after: Shared reads and writes have abortable, sequence-bound publication and stale responses cannot overwrite the active session.

independentReview.summary: Independent privacy/async review found the refresh and mutation guards sound under the focused race matrix.

historicalFindings.title: Seed changes did not generate materially different failure schedules
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Robustness analysis, competitive seeded runs, chaos exploration, and users expecting stochastic failure combinations
evidence: packages/contracts/src/index.ts defines bounded stochastic incident rules, trigger metrics, scope, cooldown, occurrence, and generated-incident caps.

packages/sim-core/src/simulate.ts deterministically compiles eligible occurrences from the scenario seed and retains each realized incident, affected nodes, correlation, occurrence, and prior-frame trigger evidence.

The full action schedule and realized stochastic evidence are bound into deterministic results/replay, while same-seed and different-seed behavior, scope compatibility, and caps have focused regressions.
historicalFindings.rootCause: There is no versioned stochastic failure distribution or deterministic incident-generation phase in the scenario and engine contracts.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Add bounded failure distributions for eligible kinds, targets, domains, timing, duration, and magnitude; compile them deterministically from the seed into an explicit event schedule that is included in run evidence and replay.
requiredTests: same seed and inputs produce an identical generated failure schedule and result
different seeds exercise materially different valid schedules
generated events respect component, region, zone, and failure-domain eligibility
replay manifest records the realized schedule
scheduled author events and generated events have deterministic precedence and caps

measurements.before: Multi-seed runs vary workload noise while authored failure timing and targets remain fixed.
measurements.after: Versioned seeded rules generate bounded, replayable and materially different eligible schedules while preserving same-input determinism.

independentReview.summary: Contracts, generated-incident physics, replay evidence, authoring controls and multi-seed regressions passed independent engine review.

historicalFindings.title: Component behavior lacked a versioned composable profile registry
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Users expecting many realistic backend technologies, maintainers adding component presets, and reviewers comparing modeled semantics
evidence: packages/sim-core/src/behavioralProfiles.ts contains ten immutable version-1 profiles spanning PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ, DynamoDB and representative AWS variants.
The contracts validate profile references and kind compatibility; simulation resolves them before frame execution and records assumptions, dated provenance, version, and local overrides per node.
Inspector apply/detach controls, share/replay round trips and completed-run manifest v3 preserve the profile reference and reject unknown, incompatible, stale or tampered evidence.
historicalFindings.rootCause: Defaults, runtime equations, editor fields, and named technology presets have no shared declarative profile contract or compatibility version.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Introduce a versioned primitive/profile registry with validated defaults, supported behaviors, editor schema, engine coefficients, failure compatibility, provenance, and migrations; keep named technologies as explicit presets composed from primitives.
requiredTests: every registered profile validates against the engine contract
profile defaults round-trip through editor, share, persistence, and replay
changing profile version changes run identity and digest
unsupported behavior or failure combinations fail closed
representative compute, cache, durable-store, queue, replica, network, and region profiles behave distinctly

measurements.before: Component semantics are encoded in scattered kind conditionals and generic node configuration.
measurements.after: A bounded immutable registry composes named presets from existing primitives and binds versioned profile evidence to simulation and replay identity.

independentReview.summary: Focused contract, profile, simulator, solver, Inspector, share and completed-run tests passed, including state-capability and tamper cases.

historicalFindings.title: The Decision Workbench inflated the initial Lab route bundle
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: First-time and resource-constrained visitors opening the Lab
evidence: The historical baseline measured the Lab chunk at 417.19 kB, 118.12 kB gzip.

apps/web/src/components/DecisionWorkbenchBoundary.tsx dynamically imports the heavy workbench only after first open, preserves the mounted instance, and exposes accessible loading/error/retry/focus restoration.

At the split point, the Lab chunk fell from 465,620 to 383,627 bytes raw and from 132,986 to 111,468 bytes deterministic gzip; the final feature-complete build keeps the boundary with Lab at 408.02 kB raw and 117.91 kB gzip and Decision Workbench deferred at 106.56 kB raw and 29.43 kB gzip.
The production manifest records the workbench as a Lab dynamic import, and offline asset preparation includes the deferred module.
historicalFindings.rootCause: Code splitting stops at route boundaries even though several heavy Lab tools are modal, secondary, or investigation-only.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Measure the current bundle and split optional Lab surfaces such as Decision Workbench, command tools, and investigation-only diagnostics behind stable lazy boundaries while preloading only when user intent is clear.
requiredTests: production bundle budget with per-chunk sizes
cold Lab interaction does not request unopened optional tools
opening every lazy surface succeeds online and from the installed offline cache
loading and error boundaries remain keyboard accessible
Core Web Vitals and parse/execute profiling at target devices

measurements.before: Historical Lab chunk: 417.19 kB, 118.12 kB gzip.
measurements.after: The isolated split saved 81,993 bytes raw and 21,518 bytes gzip at implementation time; the final feature-complete build retains the dynamic boundary and keeps optional decision tools out of initial Lab evaluation.

independentReview.summary: Boundary tests, TypeScript, production build, manifest inspection, offline packaging and Sites contracts passed; target-device Core Web Vitals and every-lazy-surface installed-offline profiling remain unexecuted.

historicalFindings.title: The install manifest has no maskable application icon
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Users installing SystemForge on launchers that apply adaptive icon masks
evidence: apps/web/public/manifest.webmanifest declares 192x192 and 512x512 PNG icons with purpose set only to any.
No separate safe-zone-tested maskable asset or purpose=maskable entry exists.
historicalFindings.rootCause: The existing elephant artwork was reused as a standard icon without a maskable-safe composition and manifest entry.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Create a dedicated maskable icon with the required safe zone, retain standard any-purpose icons, and validate installation previews across adaptive mask shapes.
requiredTests: manifest includes valid any and maskable 192 and 512 assets
maskable safe-zone preview does not crop the mark
production MIME and cache headers serve every icon
installed-app smoke on at least one adaptive-icon platform

measurements.before: No maskable icon purpose was declared.
measurements.after: Unchanged in the current worktree; both manifest icons still use purpose=any.

independentReview.summary: Manifest and asset inventory confirm the residual install-icon gap.

historicalFindings.title: The product vision's AI layer had no bounded implementation
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Scenario authors translating written briefs, interviewers drafting follow-up questions, and reviewers interpreting completed canonical runs
evidence: The baseline repository had no provider configuration, AI contracts, provider adapter, authoring compiler, debrief evidence catalog, interview assistant, or credential-free provider tests.
packages/contracts/src/index.ts now defines versioned strict request and response contracts, requirement scopes, candidate-visible interview context, and exact evidence references.

apps/api/src/aiProvider.ts, aiCompilation.ts and aiDebrief.ts keep provider credentials server-side, compile quoted numeric intent through deterministic validation, preserve private rubric scope, and allow debrief observations to cite only bounded deterministic run evidence.

apps/web/src/components/AiAssistantPanels.tsx exposes explicit preview/apply, canonical-run debrief, and phase-aware interviewer facilitation while the capability remains optional and disabled by default.
historicalFindings.rootCause: The deterministic engine and product workflows were implemented, but no trust boundary existed for optional nondeterministic assistance.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Add a disabled-by-default server-side provider boundary that returns strict intent, deterministically grounds metrics, operators, units and source spans, projects candidate-safe context, cites exact modeled evidence, and never invokes or replaces simulation physics.
requiredTests: partial or invalid provider configuration fails closed without exposing credentials
requirements reject ungrounded metrics, comparators, numbers and incompatible units
full-scenario proposals retain unspecified incidents and public or private objectives
candidate debrief and interview prompts exclude hidden rubric content and unrelated shared-run evidence
malformed, oversized, aborted and timeout provider responses fail with bounded upstream errors
browser proposals never mutate a draft before an explicit validated Apply action
stale authoring, debrief and interview responses are canceled or ignored

measurements.before: No AI capability, provider boundary or related verification existed.
measurements.after: A versioned optional layer now covers requirement compilation, scenario authoring, evidence-linked debrief and phase-aware interview facilitation without changing deterministic engine output or local availability.

independentReview.summary: Independent API privacy/security and web reviews drove closure of hidden-score leakage, cross-share binding, destructive replacement, grounding, cancellation, response bounds and stale-state defects; fake-provider and integrated tests passed, while no real provider transaction was attempted.

historicalFindings.title: Release evidence lacked mutation, stability and tracked browser acceptance gates
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Maintainers reviewing test strength, deterministic behavior, browser regressions and release confidence
evidence: The baseline had coverage reporting but no targeted mutation runner, deterministic order/concurrency stability harness, or tracked self-starting browser acceptance command.
scripts/run-targeted-mutations.mjs applies four in-memory critical-boundary mutants and requires existing assertions to kill each one.
scripts/run-test-stability.mjs reruns the non-performance suite serially and in parallel with fixed seeds and no hidden retries.

scripts/browser-acceptance.mjs builds, starts an isolated Edge profile, checks desktop and mobile routes, exercises run/pause/step/intervention/resume/trace playback, keyboard, reduced motion and warm offline behavior, records artifacts, and cleans up.
.github/workflows/ci.yml makes hardening and Windows Edge browser jobs prerequisites of container packaging and integration.
historicalFindings.rootCause: High aggregate coverage did not independently prove assertion quality, deterministic order stability or full browser workflow behavior.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Add bounded targeted mutation, serial/parallel fixed-seed stability and self-contained real-browser acceptance gates, then bind them into CI before immutable image creation.
requiredTests: each targeted mutant is rejected by an existing externally meaningful assertion
serial and parallel suites pass under distinct fixed seeds without retry
desktop and 390-pixel browser flows complete without console errors or document overflow
keyboard, reduced-motion and warm-offline checks produce reviewable artifacts
CI cannot package release images until hardening and browser jobs pass

measurements.before: No mutation, stability or tracked browser acceptance scripts were available.
measurements.after: Four targeted mutants were killed by assertions; serial and parallel 52-file, 408-test stability runs passed without retry; Edge passed all 17 route audits and nine interaction groups with zero unexpected console/network errors or acceptance defects.

independentReview.summary: Mutation, fixed-seed stability, browser startup, desktop/mobile/offline workflows, artifact emission and cleanup all passed locally and gate downstream CI jobs.

historicalFindings.title: A successful main push could reuse persistent approval and mutate production
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Production availability, release operators, reviewers of the no-deploy boundary and every public visitor
evidence: The previous deploy workflow staged every successful same-repository main push and could deploy when persistent repository variables remained enabled.

.github/workflows/deploy-hetzner.yml is now workflow_dispatch-only and requires an exact current-main SHA, the numeric successful same-repository main-push CI run ID, and the exact one-time confirmation phrase.
The validate job binds both the referenced CI run and the executing workflow ref and SHA before artifact access, environment entry or production-secret references.
scripts/stage_hetzner.sh exits before mutation without the ephemeral confirmation and never closes Caddy or stops a running release on an unauthorized invocation.
historicalFindings.rootCause: Deployment authorization was modeled as persistent repository state attached to an automatic main-push workflow instead of an exact-revision operator decision.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Require a manual protected-environment dispatch tied to the exact successful CI artifact and still-current main revision, and fail closed before any host mutation when authorization or provenance is absent.
requiredTests: main pushes cannot invoke staging or deployment
wrong confirmation, branch, executing SHA, CI run, repository, event, status or superseded main fails before artifact and secret access
stage exits before mutation when the ephemeral confirmation is absent
superseded releases fail rather than being treated as a successful skip
both host mutation jobs retain protected production-environment approval

measurements.before: A successful main push could enter staging and persistent variables could authorize public deployment.
measurements.after: Only a manual exact-revision dispatch can reach protected mutation jobs; unauthorized or superseded attempts fail before changing host state.

independentReview.summary: Focused workflow, shell, YAML and ordering contracts passed, including the adversarial dispatch-from-another-branch case. No deployment, push, secret access or external mutation occurred.

historicalFindings.title: Completed local runs disappeared after the current session
historicalFindings.affectedUsersOrWorkflows: Learners and interview candidates comparing repeated experiments, preserving a baseline, or reopening a verified replay
evidence: The baseline retained only the latest completed artifact in memory and required manual replay-file management across reloads.
Official Grafana k6, Gremlin and AWS Well-Architected workflows preserve comparisons, historical reports or milestones, making a bounded local history the closest product-adjacent gap.

apps/web/src/lib/runHistory.ts stores compact candidate-safe records and verified replay bundles in IndexedDB with a fallback for unsupported environments, serialized cross-tab mutations and explicit retention limits.

apps/web/src/components/RunHistoryPanel.tsx exposes search, star, annotate, delete, clear, verify/replay, exact comparison, compatible trends and JSON or Markdown comparison export inside the existing Decision Workbench.
Private interviewer runs, credentials, collaboration state, AI output, full frames, events, traces and reports are excluded; replay payloads are reparsed and digest-verified before use.
historicalFindings.rootCause: Run evidence was designed as a single-session artifact and replay portability was file-driven rather than indexed for repeated local experiments.
historicalFindings.proposedChange: Persist a small candidate-safe local Run library that reuses the replay integrity boundary, deduplicates identical deterministic outputs, preserves divergent outputs, and compares only semantically equivalent objectives.
requiredTests: private interview material never creates or enters a history record or export
identical inputs and results deduplicate while divergent results remain visible
retention, byte, replay-size and star caps are enforced without destructive cleanup on transient storage failure
replay payloads reject tampering before replay or download
objective deltas are toned only when candidate-visible objective semantics match
the real browser records a completed run and exposes Verify and replay from Runs

measurements.before: Completed local evidence was latest-only in memory and Report explicitly required manual download for persistence.
measurements.after: The browser retains at most 24 candidate-safe records, 20 MB total, 2 MB per replay, 30 days for unstarred entries and 6 stars, with explicit per-entry and clear-all deletion.

independentReview.summary: Independent storage, privacy and comparison review found no surviving P0-P2 after cleanup atomicity and objective-semantic regressions were added; focused, integrated and Edge workflows passed.
